newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA'S MASIRE OUTLINES DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA'S MASIRE OUTLINES DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES.

text.p: Botswana President Ketumile Masire on Monday pledged to make his public service lean and effective under a proposed five-year development plan.
Outlining economic and development priorities, he told parliament the Directorate of Public Service Management would review staffing levels in all government departments.
"The goal is a lean, but efficient public service," Masire said.

"Unless measures are put in place to control the growth of the public service we may later find ourselves in a situation where we have to take harsh measures such as retrenchment or down-sizing," he cautioned.
The country's National Development Plan 8 (NDP8) will cover a five-year period from the 1997/98 financial year, which starts in April 1997.
Masire said preliminary projections of growth under NDP8 were 4.7 percent per annum.

Without naming any specific opportunities, Masire said the government would examine the privatisation of some of its activities so that it could focus on investmenting in areas which would not interest the private sector.
He also indicated an early financial restructuring of the loss-making Botswana Railways, saying:
"The organisation has embarked on a comprehensive restructuring exercise. Proposals for appropriate financial restructuring are under active consideration by government."
Masire said his government recognised that the role of the private sector would be pivotal in implementing the NDP8 plan.

"To strengthen the private sector, we will continue our strategies of maintaining the right combination of wage rates, tax levels, interest rates, exchange rates and deregulation," the Botswana president said.
